source_message.text:
Hi Abdulbari,

This is exciting to finally see as a complete wordmark. I completely agree; this feels like a very important milestone, and seeing everything together immediately clarifies where I'd like to focus next.

The Hero V and the É accent are heading in a really good direction. One refinement I'd still love to make is ensuring the terminal of the Hero V and the É accent terminate at exactly the same height. If the accent is truly a literal slice of the Hero V, I think those highest points should align perfectly.

Looking at the wordmark as a whole, I realized my attention is no longer on the Hero V—it's on the remaining letters.

The E and L feel like they're speaking a different language than the Hero V. The small flared terminals immediately reminded me of the Roman flare direction we intentionally moved away from. I'd love for the Es and Ls to feel as custom and architectural as the Hero V rather than looking like they came from an existing typeface.

I also think the second V has lost a little of its proprietary character. In the isolated studies, I loved the subtle additional reach on the right arm. It was almost imperceptible, but it made the letter feel uniquely Vellvé. I'd love to carry that same gesture back into the wordmark.

Overall, I think we've reached exactly the point we hoped to reach. The Hero V has done its job. Now it's time for the rest of the wordmark to rise to the same standard.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
I have spent the last few hours integrating the specific design rules you outlined, and I am pleased to present this updated construction blueprint for the full VELLVÉ wordmark.

Key Refinements Presented in this Blueprint:

Peak Alignment (Top Guides): I have technically adjusted the accent's position. The highest point of the É accent now aligns mathematically with the precise vertical peak of the Hero V’s terminal, fulfilling that rule of literal continuity.

Architectural E & L Forms: To solve the 'Roman Flare' issue, I have custom-drawn the E and L. They are no longer standard serifs; they are bespoke, structured forms that now speak the language of the Anchor V. The terminals are flat, precise architectural shears (cuts), derived directly from the clean sheared edge of the Hero V’s terminal.

Restored Proprietary V: I have swapped out the middle generic V and restored the unique character we established. The middle 'V' now carries that proud, subtle upward sweep and specific right-arm reach, making it feel distinctly Vellvé.

Seeing these rules unified gives me complete confidence that the wordmark finally lives as one language. I can't wait to hear how this revised architectural blueprint resonates with you

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Abdulbari,

I really like the direction this is taking, and I think your annotations show that we're now solving the right problems.

As I looked through your construction sheet, I had two additional observations that I think will strengthen the hierarchy of the wordmark.

First, regarding the Hero V and the É accent: I don't think I communicated this clearly before. My intention isn't for the accent to begin where the Hero V terminates. Instead, I'd love for the highest point of the Hero V's right arm and the highest point of the É accent to align perfectly. If you placed a ruler across the very top of both gestures, they would land on the exact same horizontal line. To me, that creates a beautiful visual relationship between the beginning and the end of the wordmark while reinforcing that the accent is literally derived from the Hero V.

Second, I'd love to explore the hierarchy of the second V. I don't want it to simply match the cap height of the surrounding letters. Instead, I imagine it sitting slightly above the E and L characters, while still remaining below both the Hero V and the É accent. It becomes a quiet echo of the Hero V—subtle enough that it doesn't compete, but intentional enough to continue carrying that signature gesture through the wordmark.

I don't see these as new concepts—just refinements to the hierarchy we've already built.

value_updates.alignment_basis: The absolute highest points of the Hero V right arm and É accent must fall on the exact same horizontal line, rather than the accent beginning where the Hero V terminates.

Hi Brittany,

I have taken those final structural guidelines and updated the vector geometry. I am incredibly proud to present the refined, clean version of the VELLVÉ wordmark.

Here is how these final refinements have brought the entire identity together:

The Shared Horizon: The absolute highest peak of the Hero V’s sweeping right arm and the top of the É accent now align flush on the exact same horizontal line. It creates an incredibly satisfying, high-end geometric frame that grounds the beginning and end of the brand mark.

The Rhythmic V2 Echo: The middle V now breaks the standard cap-height of the E and L. It steps up quietly to act as an intentional, mid-word echo of the Hero V’s energy, adding a beautiful wave to the "skyline" of the letters before settling back down.

Pristine Architecture: The E and L characters maintain their custom, un-flared horizontal shears, ensuring every single letter feels bespoke and intentionally designed for Vellvé.

To me, this feels like the definitive, locked-in signature of the brand. I would love to hear your thoughts on how this final balance feels to you

In other words, I'd like the accent and the surrounding type to adapt to the Hero V—not the Hero V to adapt to the wordmark.

Once the approved Hero V is back in place, I think we can evaluate the rest of the typeface from there.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Abdulbari,

This is exactly the type of study I was hoping for. Thank you for working through this with me. Isolating the height variable finally allowed me to evaluate what I was actually seeing in my mind.

I would like to move forward using the 2% increase as our new baseline. I think it gives the Hero V just the right amount of quiet elevation without becoming overstated.

Before we continue, I noticed a few elements that I believe were unintentionally unlocked during this study. These were previously established design rules that I'd like to restore.

1\. The É accent should be an exact copy of the Hero V's right arm terminal.

It shouldn't be reinterpreted independently. The Hero V remains the master geometry, and the accent should simply inherit that exact form.

2\. The peak of the É accent should terminate at the exact same height as the Hero V's right arm.

That relationship has become an important part of the visual language, so I'd like those two elements to align perfectly.

3\. The second V should remain much more restrained.

The second V should absolutely carry this same design language, but much more quietly. The percentage increase should be calculated relative to the second V's original height, not interpreted visually to match the Hero V. I would like its right arm to extend proportionally above the alphabet, yet remain almost imperceptible to the eye. Right now it has become too expressive. The second V should never compete with the Hero V—it should simply echo it.
For the next comparison, I think it would be very helpful to add three reference lines:

The current reference line showing the calibrated increase from the original baseline.
A reference line through the peak of the Hero V's right arm so I can immediately verify that the É accent aligns perfectly.
A reference line at the cap height of the rest of the alphabet so we can precisely refine how far above the alphabet the second V extends.

I think we're no longer searching for new ideas. We're refining relationships between the three signature elements that define the identity. Those relationships will become one of the subtle details that people never consciously notice, but instinctively recognize.

Thank you again. I genuinely feel like we're getting very close.
